translations.idiomatic: The river-defense commander, the Earl of Wujing Zhao Hongze, and Censor-in-chief Chen Shiliang met them and were routed with countless dead.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊治舟孟瀆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the bandits fitted out boats at Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels outfitted their fleet at Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 完等至鎮江，留鉞防守，令恭以騎駐江北，暉、永以舟趨江陰，完率都指揮孫文、傅鎧趨福山港。

translations.literal: Wan and others reached Zhenjiang, left Qiu to defend, ordered Gong with cavalry to hold north of the river, Hui and Yong with boats toward Jiangyin, Wan leading Commanders Sun Wen and Fu Kai toward Fushan Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Wan reached Zhenjiang, left Qiu Yue to hold the line, posted Wen Gong's horsemen north of the river, sent Liu Hui and Xi Yong by water toward Jiangyin, and himself led Commanders Sun Wen and Fu Kai to Fushan Harbor.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，抵通州。

translations.literal: The bandits were afraid and reached Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing encirclement, the rebels made for Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 颶風大作，棄舟走保狼山。

translations.literal: A typhoon rose violently; they abandoned boats and fled to hold Lang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce hurricane struck; they abandoned their boats and fled ashore to fortify Lang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 完命同知羅瑋夜導軍登山南蹙之。

translations.literal: Wan ordered Vice Prefect Luo Wei to guide troops by night up the mountain's south to press them.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had Vice Prefect Luo Wei lead the army by night up the southern slope to hem them in.

sentences.zh: 彥名中槍死，七中矢亦赴水死，余賊盡平。

translations.literal: Yanming was shot and died; Seven was struck by arrows and also threw himself into the water and died; remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yanming fell to a musket ball, Liu Seven, pierced by arrows, drowned himself as well, and the last rebels were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 還朝，進完太子少保左都御史，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: Returning to court, Wan was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-chief; his son was ennobled hereditary commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court Wan was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-chief, and his son received hereditary appointment in the Embroidered Uniform Guard for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年代何鑒為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced He Jian as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he succeeded He Jian as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 完有才智，急功名，善交權勢。

translations.literal: Wan had talent and wisdom, was urgent for fame and merit, and was skilled at befriending the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and ambitious, Wan hungered for reputation and cultivated ties with men in power.

sentences.zh: 劉暉、許泰、江彬皆其部將，後並寵幸用事，完遂行其力。

translations.literal: Liu Hui, Xu Tai, and Jiang Bin were all his subordinate generals; later all won favor and held power, and Wan then exercised their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, Xu Tai, and Jiang Bin had served under him; when they later rose to imperial favor, Wan drew on their influence in turn.

sentences.zh: 時宸濠已萌異志。

translations.literal: At this time Chen Hao had already nursed rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: By then Prince Ning Chen Hao was already harboring treasonous intent.

sentences.zh: 聞完為兵部，致書盛陳舊好，欲復護衛及屯田。

translations.literal: Hearing Wan was at the Ministry of War, he wrote at length of old friendship, wishing to restore guard troops and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wan headed the Ministry of War, he sent a lavish letter recalling their old intimacy and asking that his guard and military colonies be restored.

sentences.zh: 完答書，令以祖制為詞。

translations.literal: Wan replied citing ancestral institutions as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Wan answered with the language of ancestral law as his excuse.

sentences.zh: 宸濠遂遣人輦金帛巨萬，寓所善教坊臧賢家，遍遺用事貴人，屬錢寧為內主。

translations.literal: Chen Hao then sent men with carts of gold and silks in the tens of thousands, lodged at his favorite, entertainment-house performer Zang Xian's home, bestowing widely on powerful courtiers in office, commissioning Qian Ning as inside patron.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao then carted tens of thousands in gold and silk to the house of the entertainer Zang Xian, whom he favored, distributing gifts among the men who held sway at court and putting Qian Ning forward as his patron within the palace.

sentences.zh: 比奏下，完遂為復請，而以屯田屬戶部，請付廷議。

translations.literal: When the memorial came down, Wan then pleaded restoration for him, but assigned military colonies to the Ministry of Revenue and requested court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial reached him, Wan petitioned for the prince's guard to be restored while referring the colonies to the Ministry of Revenue and asking that the matter be debated at court.

sentences.zh: 內閣擬旨上，並予之。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat drafted an edict and both were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat drew up an edict granting both requests.

sentences.zh: 舉朝嘩然。

translations.literal: The whole court was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Outrage swept the entire court.

sentences.zh: 六科給事中高淓、十三道御史汪賜等力爭，章並下部，久不覆。

translations.literal: Six Offices censors Gao Qing, thirteen circuits investigating censor Wang Ci and others struggled fiercely; memorials were sent to ministries but long went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Censors of the Six Offices, Gao Qing among them, and investigating censors from thirteen circuits led by Wang Ci protested vehemently; their memorials went to the ministries and languished without reply.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中徐文溥繼言之，完乃請納諫官言，帝竟不許。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretary Xu Wenpu spoke again; Wan then asked to accept the remonstrators' words; the emperor ultimately would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing supervising secretary Xu Wenpu took up the charge again; Wan then asked to heed the remonstrators, but the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 十年改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was moved to head the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，就執。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled he was promptly captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Hao rose in rebellion he was seized at once.

sentences.zh: 中官張永至南昌，搜其籍，得完平日交通事，上之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Zhang Yong reached Nanchang, searched his records, obtained Wan's usual correspondence, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Yong arrived at Nanchang, searched the prince's archives, found Wan's routine correspondence with him, and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 還至通州，執完。

translations.literal: Returning to Tongzhou he arrested Wan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march to Tongzhou he had Wan arrested.

sentences.zh: 收其母妻子女，封識其家。

translations.literal: He seized his mother, wife, children, and daughters, and sealed and inventoried his house.
translations.idiomatic: He took Wan's mother, wife, sons, and daughters into custody and sealed his household for inventory.

sentences.zh: 比還京，反縛之竿，揭姓名於首，雜俘囚中，列凱旋前部以入，將置極刑。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he bound Wan reversed on a pole, posted his name on his head, mixed him among captive prisoners, placed him in the vanguard of the triumphal entry, intending extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital he bound Wan head-down on a pole, labeled him by name, marched him among the captives at the front of the victory procession, and prepared the harshest penalty.

sentences.zh: 值武宗崩，世宗立，法司復奏完交外藩而遺金不卻，處護衛而執奏不堅，當斬。

translations.literal: As Emperor Wuzong died and Emperor Shizong acceded, the judiciary again reported Wan had dealings with an outer fief yet did not refuse gold, handled guard restoration yet did not firmly memorialize — deserving decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong died and Emperor Shizong succeeded; the judiciary again charged that Wan had trafficked with an outer prince, accepted gold without refusal, and failed to stand firm on the guard question — crimes warranting decapitation.

sentences.zh: 完復乞哀，下廷臣覆讞。

translations.literal: Wan again begged mercy; the case was sent for court ministers to re-examine.
translations.idiomatic: Wan pleaded once more for his life, and the case was referred to the assembled ministers for rehearing.

sentences.zh: 以平賊功，在八議之列，遂得減死，戍福建靖海衛。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying bandits he was within the eight considerations; death was reduced and he was exiled to Fujian Jinghai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his service in crushing the rebels he fell under the eight mitigations; his sentence was reduced from death to exile at Jinghai Guard in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 母年九十余，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: His mother was over ninety and died in prison in the end.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, past ninety, died in custody at last.

sentences.zh: 初，完嘗夢至一山曰「大武」。

translations.literal: Earlier Wan had dreamed of reaching a mountain called "Great Martial."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Wan had dreamed he came to a mountain named Great Martial.

sentences.zh: 及抵戍所，有山如其名，嘆曰：「吾戍已久定，何所逃乎！

translations.literal: When he reached the exile post there was a mountain of that name; he sighed: "My exile was long since fixed — where could I flee!
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his place of exile he found a mountain of that very name and sighed, "My banishment was settled long ago — where could I escape?

sentences.zh: 」竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: " He died at the exile post in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in exile at last.

sentences.zh: 洪鐘，字宣之，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Hong Zhong, styled Xuanzhi, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhong, whose style was Xuanzhi, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 為刑部主事，遷郎中，奉命安輯江西、福建流民。

translations.literal: He was a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, promoted to director, and ordered to settle migrants in Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, rose to director, and was dispatched to pacify displaced people in Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 還言福建武平、上杭、清流、永定，江西安遠、龍南，廣東程鄉皆流移錯雜，習鬥爭，易亂，宜及平時令有司立鄉社學，教之《詩》《書》禮讓。

translations.literal: On return he reported that Fujian Wuping, Shanghang, Qingliu, Yongding, Jiangxi Anyuan, Longnan, Guangdong Chengxiang all had mixed migrants, practiced fighting, were prone to disorder — in peaceful times officials should establish village community schools teaching the Odes, Documents, ritual and deference.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he warned that in Wuping, Shanghang, Qingliu, and Yongding in Fujian, Anyuan and Longnan in Jiangxi, and Chengxiang in Guangdong migrants were intermingled, quarrelsome, and ripe for rebellion; in quiet times local officials ought to found village schools and teach the Odes, Documents, and the rites of courtesy.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，再遷四川按察使。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he was again promoted to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Hongzhi reign he was promoted again, to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 馬湖土知府安鰲恣淫虐，土人怨之刺骨，有司利其金置不問，遷延二十年。

translations.literal: Ma Lake native-official prefect An Ao was wantonly lewd and cruel; natives hated him to the bone; officials profited from his gold and ignored it — this dragged on twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: At Ma Lake the native prefect An Ao ruled with unrestrained lust and cruelty; the tribespeople loathed him, yet officials, greedy for his bribes, looked away until twenty years had passed.

sentences.zh: 僉事曲銳請巡按御史張鸞按治，鐘贊決，捕鰲送京師，置極刑。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Qu Rui asked Investigating Censor Zhang Luan to investigate and punish; Zhong endorsed the decision, Ao was arrested and sent to the capital, and subjected to extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Qu Rui asked Investigating Censor Zhang Luan to take the case; Zhong backed the move, and Ao was seized, sent to the capital, and executed.

sentences.zh: 安氏自唐以來世有馬湖，至是改流官，一方始靖。

translations.literal: The An clan had held Ma Lake since Tang times; now it was changed to regular officials, and the region was pacified at last.
translations.idiomatic: The An family had ruled Ma Lake since the Tang; with the post turned over to appointed officials, the area finally knew peace.

sentences.zh: 歷江西、福建左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served through the posts of left and right provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the left and right provincial administration commissions of Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十一年擢右副都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 整飭薊州邊備，建議增築塞垣。

translations.literal: He put in order the frontier defenses of Jizhou and proposed adding and repairing the border wall.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the Jizhou frontier and urged the extension of the border ramparts.

sentences.zh: 自山海關西北至密雲古北口、黃花鎮直抵居庸，延亙千餘里，繕復城堡二百七十所，悉城緣邊諸縣，因奏減防秋兵六千人，歲省挽輸犒賚費數萬計。

translations.literal: From northwest of Shanhaiguan through Gubeikou of Miyun and Huanghua garrison straight to Juyong, extending more than a thousand li, he repaired two hundred seventy castles, walled all frontier counties, and memorialized to reduce six thousand autumn-defense troops, saving tens of thousands in transport and reward costs each year.
translations.idiomatic: From northwest of Shanhaiguan through Miyun's Gubeikou and Huanghua garrison to Juyong—over a thousand li—he restored two hundred seventy forts, walled every frontier county, and won approval to cut six thousand autumn-defense troops, saving tens of thousands yearly in transport and reward expenses.

sentences.zh: 所部潮河川去京師二百里，居兩山間，廣百余丈，水漲成巨浸，水退則坦然平陸，寇得長驅直入。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction the Chaohu River lay two hundred li from the capital between two mountains, more than a hundred zhang wide when flooded into a great lake, and when the water withdrew a level plain where raiders could charge straight through.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaohu River in his charge stood two hundred li from the capital between two hills; when swollen it became a vast flood, and when it fell it left open ground over which enemies could gallop straight in.

sentences.zh: 鐘言：「關以東三里許，其山外高內庳，約余二丈，可鑿為兩渠，分殺水勢，而於口外斜築石堰以束水。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "About three li east of the pass the mountain is high outside and low inside, leaving roughly two zhang; two channels could be cut to divide the water's force, and outside the mouth a slanting stone weir built to confine the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong argued that three li east of the pass the hills rose outside and dipped within, leaving about two zhang of height where two channels could be cut to split the current, with a slanting stone weir below to hold the water back.

sentences.zh: 置關堰內，守以百人，使寇不得馳突，可免京師北顧憂，且得屯種河堧地。

translations.literal: Place the pass inside the weir, garrison it with a hundred men, so raiders cannot burst through, the capital's northern worry may be removed, and the river-bank land may be farmed.
translations.idiomatic: With the pass set behind the weir and a hundred men to hold it, raiders could be stopped from breaking through, the capital spared its northern anxiety, and the river flats put under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書馬文升等請從之。

translations.literal: " The Minister of War Ma Wensheng and others asked to follow his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Ma Wensheng and others petitioned to adopt his plan.

sentences.zh: 比興工，鑿山，山石崩，壓死者數百人。

translations.literal: When work began and the mountain was cut, the rock collapsed and several hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once construction started and the hills were cut, the rock gave way and buried several hundred workers.

sentences.zh: 御史弋福、給事中馬予聰等劾鐘。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Yi Fu, supervising secretary Ma Yucong, and others impeached Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Yi Fu and Supervising Secretary Ma Yucong impeached Zhong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張烜等請罷役，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan and others asked to halt the project; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan petitioned to stop the works, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，工成，侍郎張達偕司禮中官往視。

translations.literal: Before long the work was finished; Vice Minister Zhang Da went with a eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the project was done, and Vice Minister Zhang Da went with a palace eunuch to inspect it.

sentences.zh: 還言石洞僅泄小水，地近邊垣多沙石，不利耕種。

translations.literal: On return they reported the stone channels released only a trickle, the ground near the border wall was mostly sand and stone, and ill suited to farming.
translations.idiomatic: They returned saying the stone channels let through only a trickle and that the soil near the wall was sandy and stony, poor for planting.

sentences.zh: 給事中屈伸等劾鐘欺妄三罪，諸言官及兵部皆請逮鐘。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Qu Shen and others impeached Zhong on three counts of fraud; remonstrating officials and the Ministry of War all asked that Zhong be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qu Shen charged Zhong with three counts of deceit, and censors and the Ministry of War alike demanded his arrest.

sentences.zh: 帝以鐘為國繕邊，不當罪，停俸三月。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zhong had repaired the frontier for the state, said he should not be punished and stopped his salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Zhong had fortified the border for the realm and ought not be punished; his salary was withheld for three months.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，由巡撫貴州召督漕運兼巡撫江北。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, from grand coordinator of Guizhou he was summoned to superintend grain transport and concurrently grand coordinate the north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was recalled from Guizhou to direct the grain transport and oversee the north bank.

sentences.zh: 明年就進右都御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced in place to Right Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted on the spot to Right Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、浙江運舟由下港口及孟瀆河溯大江以達瓜洲，遠涉二百八十餘里，往往遭風濤。

translations.literal: Transport boats from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Zhejiang went from Xiaogangkou and the Mengdu River up the great river to Guazhou, a distant haul of more than two hundred eighty li, often meeting wind and waves.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Zhejiang had to ascend the Yangzi from Xiaogangkou and the Mengdu River to Guazhou—a run of more than two hundred eighty li, often battered by wind and tide.

sentences.zh: 鐘言：「孟瀆對江有夾河，可抵白塔河口。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Facing Mengdu on the river is a channel that can reach Baieta River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong reported that across from Mengdu lay a channel that could reach the mouth of the Baieta River.

sentences.zh: 舊置四閘，徑四十里。

translations.literal: Formerly four locks were set along forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Four locks had once been placed along forty li.

sentences.zh: 至宜陵鎮再折而北，即抵揚州運河。

translations.literal: At Yiling town it turned north again and then reached the Yangzhou canal.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiling it bent north once more and joined the Yangzhou canal.

sentences.zh: 開浚為便。

translations.literal: To dredge it would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging it would shorten the route.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 改掌南京都察院，就遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to head the Nanjing Censorate and then promoted to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to head the Nanjing Censorate and soon made Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，加太子少保兼左都御史，掌院事。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Censor-in-chief, directing the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year's winter he was named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-chief, presiding over the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 五年春，湖廣歲饑盜起。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year famine struck Huguang and bandits rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's spring Huguang suffered famine and rebels broke out.

sentences.zh: 命鐘以本官總制軍務，陜西、河南、四川亦隸焉。

translations.literal: Zhong was ordered in his existing post to assume overall military command, with Shaanxi, Henan, and Sichuan also under him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was commanded to take overall charge of operations, with Shaanxi, Henan, and Sichuan placed under his authority as well.

sentences.zh: 沔陽賊楊清、丘仁等僭稱天王、將軍，出沒洞庭間。

translations.literal: Mianyang bandits Yang Qing, Qiu Ren, and others presumptuously styled themselves Heavenly King and General, ranging over Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: The Mianyang rebels Yang Qing and Qiu Ren proclaimed themselves Heavenly King and General and roamed the Dongting region.

sentences.zh: 圍岳州，陷臨湘，官軍屢失利。

translations.literal: They besieged Yuezhou, took Linxiang, and government troops repeatedly lost.
translations.idiomatic: They encircled Yuezhou, seized Linxiang, and government forces met defeat again and again.

sentences.zh: 鐘及總兵官毛倫檄都指揮潘勛、柴奎，布政使陳鎬，副使蔣昇擊破之於麻穰灘，擒斬七百四十余人，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Zhong and overall commander Mao Lun ordered Commanders Pan Xun and Chai Kui, Administration Commissioner Chen Hao, and Vice Commissioner Jiang Sheng to rout them at Mahang Beach, capturing and slaying more than seven hundred forty; the bandits were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Commander-in-chief Mao Lun sent Commanders Pan Xun and Chai Kui with Administration Commissioner Chen Hao and Vice Commissioner Jiang Sheng to crush the rebels at Mahang Beach, killing or capturing over seven hundred forty, after which the uprising collapsed.

sentences.zh: 初，鐘掌院事，劉瑾方熾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong directed the court, Liu Jin was at the height of power.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong first headed the Censorate, Liu Jin was at the height of his power.

sentences.zh: 及瑾誅，言官劾鐘徇瑾撻御史。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, remonstrating officials impeached Zhong for yielding to Jin and flogging a censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall, censors accused Zhong of pandering to Jin and having a fellow censor beaten.

sentences.zh: 朝議以鐘討賊，置不問。

translations.literal: Court debate held that Zhong was suppressing bandits and let the matter pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided Zhong was still needed against the rebels and took no action.

sentences.zh: 時保寧賊藍廷瑞自稱順天王，鄢本恕自稱「刮地王」，其黨廖惠稱「掃地王」，眾十萬余，置四十八總管，延蔓陜西、湖廣之境。

translations.literal: At this time Baoning bandit Lan Tingrui styled himself King Shun of Heaven, Yan Benyu styled himself "King Who Scrapes the Earth," his follower Liao Hui styled "King Who Sweeps the Earth," their host exceeding one hundred thousand, with forty-eight chief stewards, spreading through Shaanxi and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Baoning rebel Lan Tingrui called himself King Shun of Heaven, Yan Benyu took the title "King Who Scrapes the Earth," and his lieutenant Liao Hui "King Who Sweeps the Earth"; their forces passed one hundred thousand, with forty-eight chiefs, and ravaged Shaanxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞與惠謀據保寧，本恕謀據漢中，取鄖陽，由荊、襄東下。

translations.literal: Tingrui and Hui plotted to hold Baoning, Benyu plotted to hold Hanzhong and take Yunyang, then go east through Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui and Hui aimed to seize Baoning while Benyu planned on Hanzhong, Yunyang, and a march east through Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林俊方議遏通江，而惠已至，攻陷其城，殺參議黃瓚，僉事錢朝鳳等遁去。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun was just debating blocking Tong River when Hui had already arrived, stormed the city, killed Vice Commissioner Huang Zan, and Vice Commissioner Qian Zhaofeng and others fled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun was still debating how to block the Tong River when Hui was already upon them, took the city, slew Vice Commissioner Huang Zan, and drove Qian Zhaofeng and others to flight.

sentences.zh: 適官軍自他郡還，賊疑援兵至，亦遁。

translations.literal: Just then government troops returned from another command; the bandits, suspecting reinforcements had come, also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops happened to be returning from another district; the rebels, mistaking them for fresh reinforcements, withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 俊益發羅、回及石矽士兵助朝鳳進剿，參議公勉仁亦會。

translations.literal: Jun further sent Luo and Hui tribesmen and Shixi native soldiers to aid Zhaofeng in pursuit; Vice Commissioner Gong Mianren also joined.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Luo and Hui tribesmen and Shixi native troops to reinforce Zhaofeng, and Vice Commissioner Gong Mianren joined the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 龍灘河漲，賊半渡，羅、回奮擊之，擒斬八百余人，墜崖溺水甚眾。

translations.literal: The Longtan River rose; half the bandits were mid-crossing when Luo and Hui struck fiercely, capturing and slaying more than eight hundred; many fell from cliffs or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the swollen Longtan ford the rebels were half across when Luo and Hui tribesmen fell on them, killing or capturing over eight hundred while many plunged from cliffs or drowned.

sentences.zh: 俊復遣知府張敏、何珊等追之，獲惠，余眾奔陜西西鄉。

translations.literal: Jun again sent prefects Zhang Min and He Shan in pursuit; Hui was taken, and the rest fled to Xixiang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Prefects Zhang Min and He Shan after them, seized Hui, and drove the remnant into Xixiang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鐘乃下令招撫，歸者萬余人。

translations.literal: Zhong then ordered pacification by recruitment, and more than ten thousand returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong proclaimed an offer of surrender, and over ten thousand came in.

sentences.zh: 既而賊收散亡，陷營山，殺僉事王源，縱掠蓬、劍二州。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits gathered the scattered and took Yingshan, killing Vice Commissioner Wang Yuan, then raided Peng and Jian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels regrouped, stormed Yingshan, slew Vice Commissioner Wang Yuan, and looted Peng and Jian.

sentences.zh: 鐘赴四川，與俊議多不合，軍機牽制，賊益熾。

translations.literal: Zhong went to Sichuan; he and Jun disagreed on many points; military affairs were entangled, and the bandits grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong entered Sichuan, clashed repeatedly with Jun over strategy, and as operations bogged down the rebellion flared worse.

sentences.zh: 已，乃檄陜西、湖廣、河南兵分道進，湖廣兵先追及於陜西石泉。

translations.literal: Later he ordered Shaanxi, Huguang, and Henan troops to advance on separate routes; Huguang troops first caught up with them at Shiquan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then directed Shaanxi, Huguang, and Henan forces along separate routes; the Huguang column first overtook the rebels at Shiquan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞走漢中，都指揮金冕圍之。

translations.literal: Tingrui fled to Hanzhong; Commander Jin Mian besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui ran for Hanzhong, where Commander Jin Mian encircled him.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫藍章方駐漢中，廷瑞遣其黨何虎詣章，乞還川就撫。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Lan Zhang was stationed at Hanzhong; Tingrui sent his follower He Hu to Zhang, begging to return to Sichuan for pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Lan Zhang of Shaanxi held Hanzhong when Tingrui sent He Hu to beg leave to return to Sichuan and accept pacification.

sentences.zh: 章以廷瑞本川賊，恐急之必致死，陜且受患，遂令冕護之出境。

translations.literal: Zhang, because Tingrui was originally a Sichuan bandit and feared pressing him would drive him to desperate measures and bring harm to Shaanxi, then ordered Mian to escort him out of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, knowing Tingrui was a Sichuan rebel at heart, feared driving him to extremes would endanger Shaanxi and told Mian to escort him across the border.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞既入川，求降，鐘等令至東鄉聽撫。

translations.literal: Once Tingrui entered Sichuan and sought surrender, Zhong and the others ordered him to come to Dongxiang to hear pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Sichuan, Tingrui offered to surrender; Zhong ordered him to Dongxiang to negotiate terms.

sentences.zh: 賊意在緩師，遷延累月，依山結營，要求營山縣或臨江市屯其眾，遣官為質。

translations.literal: The bandits intended to delay the army; months dragged on as they camped on the hills, demanding Yingshan county or Linjiang city to settle their host, and sending an official as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to stall the campaign, lingered for months in hill camps, demanded Yingshan or Linjiang to quarter their men, and insisted on a hostage from the government.

sentences.zh: 鐘令漢中通判羅賢入其營。

translations.literal: Zhong ordered Hanzhong Assistant Prefect Luo Xian to enter their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong sent Hanzhong Assistant Prefect Luo Xian into the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 本恕來謁，約既定，會官軍有殺其樵采者，賊復疑懼，遂殺賢，剽如故。

translations.literal: Benyu came to audience; the agreement was set, but when government troops killed some of their wood-gatherers the bandits again grew suspicious and fearful, then killed Xian and raided as before.
translations.idiomatic: Benyu came in to parley and terms seemed set, until soldiers killed some rebel foragers; the rebels panicked, murdered Xian, and returned to plunder.

sentences.zh: 官軍為七壘守之，賊不得逸，其黨漸潰。

translations.literal: Government troops held seven camps to block them so they could not escape; their faction gradually dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Seven government camps penned them in; their following began to crumble.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞以所掠女子詐為己女，結婚於永順土舍彭世麟，冀得間逸去。

translations.literal: Tingrui took a captured woman and pretended she was his daughter, marrying into the Yongshun native chieftain Peng Shilin's house, hoping by that means to slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui passed off a captive woman as his daughter and married into the house of the Yongshun chieftain Peng Shilin, hoping for a chance to escape.

sentences.zh: 世麟密白鐘，鐘授方略使圖之。

translations.literal: Shilin secretly informed Zhong; Zhong gave him a plan to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin secretly reported to Zhong, who furnished a stratagem.

sentences.zh: 及期，廷瑞、本恕暨其黨王金珠等二十八人鹹來會。

translations.literal: When the day came, Tingrui, Benyu, and their follower Wang Jinzhu and twenty-eight others all came to the meeting.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Tingrui, Benyu, Wang Jinzhu, and twenty-eight others all appeared.

sentences.zh: 伏發悉就擒，惟廖麻子得脫。

translations.literal: Ambushers sprang up and seized them all; only Liao Mazi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden troops seized them all; only Liao Mazi got away.

sentences.zh: 其眾聞變，驚潰渡河。

translations.literal: Their host, hearing of the change, fled in panic across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel masses, hearing what had happened, broke in panic across the river.

sentences.zh: 鐘遣兵追擊，俘斬七百余人，以功進太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhong sent troops in pursuit, capturing and slaying more than seven hundred; for merit he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's pursuers killed or captured over seven hundred more, and for this he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廖麻子及其黨曹甫掠營山、蓬州。

translations.literal: Before long Liao Mazi and his follower Cao Fu raided Yingshan and Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liao Mazi and his lieutenant Cao Fu were raiding Yingshan and Pengzhou again.

sentences.zh: 七年，總兵官楊宏，副使張敏、馬昊、何珊等合擊之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year overall commander Yang Hong and Vice Commissioners Zhang Min, Ma Hao, He Shan, and others combined to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Commander-in-chief Yang Hong with Vice Commissioners Zhang Min, Ma Hao, and He Shan joined forces against them.

sentences.zh: 賊勢蹙，鐘乃議招撫。

translations.literal: The bandits' position was tight; Zhong then debated pacification by recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed hard, Zhong turned again to offers of surrender.

sentences.zh: 敏以單騎詣甫營，甫聽命，遂赴軍門受約束，歸散其黨。

translations.literal: Min went alone on horseback to Fu's camp; Fu obeyed, then came to army headquarters to accept restraint and disbanded his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Min rode alone into Fu's camp; Fu submitted, came to headquarters under bond, and sent his men home.

sentences.zh: 而麻子忿甫背己，殺之，並其眾，轉掠川東。

translations.literal: Mazi, resenting Fu's betrayal, killed him and absorbed his host, then turned to raid eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mazi, furious at Fu's defection, slew him, took over his band, and swept through eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 官軍不敢擊，潛躡賊後，馘良民為功，土兵虐尤甚。

translations.literal: Government troops dared not strike; they secretly followed behind the bandits and claimed common people's heads for merit; native soldiers were even more brutal.
translations.idiomatic: Regular troops scarcely fought, trailing the rebels to cut off civilians' heads for credit, while native levies were worse still.

sentences.zh: 時有謠曰：「賊如梳，軍如篦，土兵如剃。

translations.literal: A saying ran: "Bandits like a comb, troops like a fine comb, native soldiers like a razor.
translations.idiomatic: People said, "The rebels comb lightly, the army combs closer, and the native soldiers shave you bare."

sentences.zh: 」巡按御史王綸、紀功御史汪景芳劾鐘縱兵不戢。

translations.literal: " Investigating Censor Wang Lun and merit-recording Censor Wang Jingfang impeached Zhong for indulging troops without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wang Lun and merit censor Wang Jingfang accused Zhong of letting his men run wild.

sentences.zh: 綸復奏鐘樂飲縱遊，致賊自合州渡江陷州縣。

translations.literal: Lun again memorialized that Zhong feasted and roamed at will, causing bandits to cross the river from Hezhou and seize prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun added that Zhong feasted and wandered while rebels crossed from Hezhou and overran towns.

sentences.zh: 詔召鐘還，以彭澤代，鐘遂乞歸。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Zhong; Peng Ze replaced him, and Zhong then asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The throne recalled Zhong, sent Peng Ze in his place, and Zhong sought retirement.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年卒，謚襄惠。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Jiajing and was given the posthumous title Xianghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jiajing and was posthumously titled Xianghui.

sentences.zh: 陳鎬，會稽人。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the twenty-third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-third year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 既平賊，就遷右副都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: Once the bandits were pacified he was promoted in place to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was made Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang on the spot.

sentences.zh: 蔣昇，祁陽人，鎬同年進士。

translations.literal: Jiang Sheng was a native of Qiyang, a jinshi of the same year as Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Sheng of Qiyang had taken the jinshi in the same year as Chen Hao.

sentences.zh: 陳金，字汝礪，應城人，徙武昌。

translations.literal: Chen Jin, styled Ruli, was a native of Yingcheng who moved to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin, whose style was Ruli, was born in Yingcheng and later moved to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 祖坦，夔州知府。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had served as prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 父琳，廣西僉事。

translations.literal: His father Lin was a vice commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin had been a vice commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 金舉成化八年進士，除婺源知縣，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Jin passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Chenghua, was appointed magistrate of Wuyuan, and promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jin passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Chenghua, became magistrate of Wuyuan, and rose to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，出按浙江，還因災異劾文武大僚十九人，侍郎丁永中、南京大理卿吳道宏、南寧伯毛文等多罷去。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he went out to inspect Zhejiang; on return, citing omens and anomalies, he impeached nineteen civil and military grandees; Vice Minister Ding Yongzhong, Nanjing chief justice of the Court of Judicial Review Wu Daohong, Earl of Nanning Mao Wen, and many others were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he inspected Zhejiang; returning, he used celestial warnings to impeach nineteen high officials, bringing down Vice Minister Ding Yongzhong, Nanjing chief justice Wu Daohong, the Earl of Nanning Mao Wen, and many others.

sentences.zh: 尋遷山西副使，歷雲南左布政使，討平竹子箐叛苗。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Shanxi vice commissioner, served through Yunnan left provincial administration commissioner, and suppressed the rebellious Miao of Zhuziqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Shanxi vice commissioner, rose to Yunnan left provincial administration commissioner, and crushed the Zhuziqing Miao revolt.

sentences.zh: 十三年，就拜右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed on the spot Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was named Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yunnan on the spot.

sentences.zh: 孟養酋思祿與孟密酋思揲構兵積年。

translations.literal: Mengyang chieftain Silu and Mengmi chieftain Siye had fought for years.
translations.idiomatic: The Mengyang chief Silu and the Mengmi chief Siye had been at war for years.

sentences.zh: 金奉詔發緬甸、幹崖、隴川、南甸諸部兵，聚糧十二萬，為征討計，而遣參議郭緒往撫之。

translations.literal: Jin received orders to raise troops from Burma, Ganyai, Longchuan, Nandian, and other departments, gather one hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain, plan a punitive campaign, and send Vice Commissioner Guo Xu to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to mobilize Burma, Ganyai, Longchuan, Nandian, and other dependencies, amass one hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain, and prepare an expedition, Jin sent Vice Commissioner Guo Xu to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 思祿懼，遂罷兵修貢，金以功賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Silu was afraid and then ceased troops and restored tribute; Jin was rewarded with silver and silks for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Silu, alarmed, stood down and renewed tribute; Jin received silver and silks in reward.

sentences.zh: 貴州兵敗賊婦米魯，米魯退攻平夷衛及大河、扼勒諸堡。

translations.literal: Guizhou troops were defeated by the bandit woman Milu; Milu withdrew and attacked Pingyi Guard and the forts of Dahe and Ele.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou forces lost to the rebel woman Milu, who then turned on Pingyi Guard and the forts of Dahe and Ele.

sentences.zh: 金發兵連破之，增俸一等，召為南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Jin sent troops and defeated them in succession, received one step in salary increase, and was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent troops, broke them in a series of battles, gained one rank in salary, and was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，給事中周璽等劾不職大臣，金與焉。

translations.literal: At the change to Zhengde, supervising secretaries Zhou Xuan and others impeached incompetent grand ministers; Jin was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde began, Supervising Secretary Zhou Xuan and others impeached negligent ministers, Jin included.

sentences.zh: 詔不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The throne took no action.

sentences.zh: 金以母老乞歸，不允。

translations.literal: Jin, because his mother was old, begged to return home; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin asked to retire to care for his aged mother but was refused.

sentences.zh: 尋以右都御史總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Censor-in-chief to supervise military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Censor-in-chief to direct the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 時內臣韋霦等建議，請輸兩廣各司所貯銀於京師。

translations.literal: At this time the inner courtier Wei Zhen and others proposed shipping silver stored in the various offices of the two Guang to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuch Wei Zhen and others proposed shipping the silver hoarded in Guang offices to the capital.

sentences.zh: 金疏不可，詔留二十余萬。

translations.literal: Jin memorialized that this could not be done; an edict left more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jin protested; the court left more than two hundred thousand in place.

sentences.zh: 馬平、洛容僮猖獗，金偕總兵官毛銳發兵十三萬征之，俘斬七千余人，進左都御史。

translations.literal: The Yao of Maping and Luorong were fierce; Jin with overall commander Mao Rui sent one hundred thirty thousand troops to campaign against them, capturing and slaying more than seven thousand, and was advanced to Left Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Maping and Luorong were rampant; Jin and Commander Mao Rui marched one hundred thirty thousand men against them, killed or captured over seven thousand, and Jin was promoted to Left Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 斷藤峽苗時出剽。

translations.literal: Miao of Duanteng Gorge often came out to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao of Duanteng Gorge raided whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 金念苗嗜魚鹽，可以利縻也，乃立約束，令民與苗市，改峽曰永通。

translations.literal: Jin thought the Miao craved fish and salt and could be bound by profit; he therefore set regulations and ordered people to trade with the Miao, renaming the gorge Yongtong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reckoned the Miao could be tamed with fish and salt, set market rules, and renamed the gorge Yongtong, "Ever Open."

sentences.zh: 苗性貪而黠，初陽受約，既乃不予直，殺掠益甚。

translations.literal: The Miao were greedy and cunning; at first they outwardly accepted the pact, then would not pay fair price and raided all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao were greedy and sly: they accepted the bargain in name, then refused fair payment and looted worse than before.

sentences.zh: 潯州人為語曰：「永通不通，來葬江中，誰其作者？

translations.literal: The people of Xun made a saying: "Yongtong does not open; come bury in the river—who made this?
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhou folk sang, "Ever Open stays shut—who gets buried in the river? Who wrought this?

sentences.zh: 噫，陳公！

translations.literal: Alas, Lord Chen!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Lord Chen!"

sentences.zh: 」蓋咎金失計也。

translations.literal: " It blamed Jin for the failed plan.
translations.idiomatic: The rhyme blamed Jin for the miscalculation.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's tenth month he became Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，召為左都御史，未聞命，以母喪歸。

translations.literal: The next winter he was summoned as Left Censor-in-chief; before the order reached him he returned home for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was called to be Left Censor-in-chief, but before the appointment arrived his mother died and he went home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，江西盜起。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year bandits rose in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's second month rebels broke out in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔起金故官，總制軍務。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Jin to his former office to assume overall military command.
translations.idiomatic: The throne recalled Jin to his old rank to take overall command of operations.

sentences.zh: 南畿、浙江、福建、廣東、湖廣文武將吏俱隸焉。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the southern capital region, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Huguang all came under him.
translations.idiomatic: Every civil and military officer from the southern capital districts through Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Huguang fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 許便宜從事，都指揮以下不用命者專刑戮。

translations.literal: He was permitted to act at discretion; commanders-in-chief and below who disobeyed orders could be executed on his sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: He could act as he saw fit, and any regional commander or subordinate who defied orders might be put to death on his word alone.

sentences.zh: 當是時，撫州則東鄉賊王鈺五、徐仰三、傅傑一、揭端三等；

translations.literal: At this time in Fuzhou were the Dongxiang bandits Wang Yuwu, Xu Yangsan, Fu Jieyi, Jie Duansan, and others;
translations.idiomatic: In Fuzhou the Dongxiang rebels included Wang Yuwu, Xu Yangsan, Fu Jieyi, and Jie Duansan;

sentences.zh: 南昌則姚源賊汪澄二、王浩八、殷勇十、洪瑞七等；

translations.literal: in Nanchang the Yaoyuan bandits Wang Chenger, Wang Haoba, Yin Yongshi, Hong Ruiqi, and others;
translations.idiomatic: in Nanchang the Yaoyuan rebels Wang Chenger, Wang Haoba, Yin Yongshi, and Hong Ruiqi;

sentences.zh: 瑞州則華林賊羅光權、陳福一等；

translations.literal: in Ruizhou the Hualin bandits Luo Guangquan, Chen Fuyi, and others;
translations.idiomatic: in Ruizhou the Hualin rebels Luo Guangquan and Chen Fuyi;

sentences.zh: 而贛州大帽山賊何積欽等又起。

translations.literal: and on Great Hat Mountain in Ganzhou the bandit He Jiqin and others also rose.
translations.idiomatic: while on Ganzhou's Great Hat Mountain He Jiqin and others rose as well.

sentences.zh: 官軍累年不能克。

translations.literal: Government troops had been unable to overcome them for years.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces had failed to crush them for years.

sentences.zh: 金以屬郡兵不足用，奏調廣西狼土兵。

translations.literal: Jin, because the troops of the subordinate command were insufficient, memorialized to transfer Guangxi wolf native soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Finding local troops inadequate, Jin asked for Guangxi wolf native levies.

sentences.zh: 明年二月先進兵東鄉，遣參議徐蕃等分屯要害，而令副總兵張勇，土官岑瑽、岑猛各統官兵、目兵擊賊熟塘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he first advanced on Dongxiang, sent Vice Commissioner Xu Fan and others to hold key points, and ordered Deputy Commander Zhang Yong and native officials Cen Cong and Cen Meng each to lead regular and native troops against the bandits at Shutang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year's second month he opened with Dongxiang, posted Vice Commissioner Xu Fan at choke points, and sent Deputy Commander Zhang Yong with native chiefs Cen Cong and Cen Meng against Shutang.

sentences.zh: 進戰南甗，追敗之赤岸蔭嶺。

translations.literal: Advancing to battle at Nanyan, he pursued and defeated them at Chian and Yinling.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyan he pressed the attack and drove them in defeat to Chian and Yinling.

sentences.zh: 擒仰三，馘鈺五等，克柵二百六十五，斬首萬一千六百余級，俘七百五十余人。

translations.literal: Yangsan was taken, Yuwu and the rest were beheaded, two hundred sixty-five stockades were taken, eleven thousand six hundred odd heads were cut, and more than seven hundred fifty were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yangsan, beheaded Yuwu and others, stormed two hundred sixty-five stockades, took eleven thousand six hundred heads, and captured over seven hundred fifty men.

sentences.zh: 五月移師姚源，令參政董樸、吳廷舉等分營余幹、安仁、貴溪、鄱陽、樂平遏賊，而親統大軍搗其巢，勇十重創死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he shifted his army to Yaoyuan, ordered Administration Commissioners Dong Pu and Wu Tingju and others to camp at Yugan, Anren, Guixi, Poyang, and Leping to block the bandits, while he personally led the main force against their lair; Yongshi died of grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he moved on Yaoyuan, set Dong Pu and Wu Tingju to block escape routes through Yugan and neighboring counties, and led the main column against the nest himself; Yin Yongshi died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 會張勇以目兵至，毒弩射殺瑞七、成七等，俘斬共五千余人。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yong arrived with native troops, poisoned crossbows shot and killed Ruiqi, Chengqi, and others; captures and slayings together exceeded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong arrived with native troops whose poisoned bolts killed Ruiqi and Chengqi; kills and captures passed five thousand.

sentences.zh: 七月乘勝斬光權。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, pressing the victory, Guangquan was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he pressed the advantage and beheaded Guangquan.

sentences.zh: 華林賊盡平。

translations.literal: The Hualin bandits were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 又督副使王秩等擊大帽山賊，獲積欽，俘斬千七百余人。

translations.literal: He also supervised Vice Commissioner Wang Zhi and others in attacking the Great Hat Mountain bandits, took Jiqin, and captured or slew more than one thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed Vice Commissioner Wang Zhi against Great Hat Mountain, seized Jiqin, and killed or captured over one thousand seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 半歲間，剿賊幾盡。

translations.literal: Within half a year the bandits were nearly all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In half a year the rebels were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 遂即東鄉立縣，並立萬年縣，招降人居之。

translations.literal: He then established a county at Dongxiang and also established Wannian county, settling surrendered people there.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a county at Dongxiang, created Wannian county, and resettled those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 前後每奏捷，輒賜璽書嘉勞，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported victory the throne sent sealed letters of praise and reward and bestowed silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Each victory brought sealed praise from the throne and gifts of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and his son ennobled hereditary commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son received hereditary rank in the Embroidered Uniform Guard for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 金累破劇賊，然所用目兵貪殘嗜殺，剽掠甚於賊，有巨族數百口闔門罹害者。

translations.literal: Jin repeatedly broke fierce bandits, yet the native troops he used were greedy, cruel, and bloodthirsty, plundering worse than the bandits; great clans of several hundred suffered whole households wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jin crushed formidable rebels, his native levies were greedy and savage, looting worse than the bandits themselves; great families of hundreds perished to the last soul.

sentences.zh: 所獲婦女率指為賊屬，載數千艘去。

translations.literal: Captured women were mostly labeled bandit kin and carried off in thousands of boats.
translations.idiomatic: Women taken in the campaigns were called rebel dependents and shipped away by the thousand in boats.

sentences.zh: 民間謠曰：「土賊猶可，土兵殺我。

translations.literal: A folk saying ran: "Bandit natives are bearable; native soldiers kill us.
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Rebel natives we can endure; the government's native soldiers kill us."

sentences.zh: 」金亦知民患之，方倚其力，不為禁。

translations.literal: " Jin also knew the people suffered from them, but relied on their strength and did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin knew the people suffered, yet he depended on their strength and did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 又不能持廉，軍資頗私入。

translations.literal: He also could not remain incorrupt; much military funds went into his private purse.
translations.idiomatic: Nor could he keep his hands clean; much of the war chest found its way into his own purse.

sentences.zh: 功雖多，士民皆深怨焉。

translations.literal: Though his merit was great, gentry and commoners alike deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His victories were many, but scholars and commoners alike deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 東鄉之役，瑽兵縱弩射，趫捷若飛，賊大窘。

translations.literal: In the Dongxiang campaign Cong's troops loosed crossbows and flew like the wind; the bandits were greatly pressed.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongxiang, Cen Cong's men shot crossbows and moved like the wind, pinning the rebels hard.

sentences.zh: 鎏兵要賞千金，金靳不予，乃縱賊使逸。

translations.literal: Meng's troops demanded a reward of a thousand gold; Jin refused to grant it, and they then let the bandits escape.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Meng's men demanded a thousand taels of gold; Jin refused, and they let the rebels slip away.

sentences.zh: 桀黠者多不死，尚數千人。

translations.literal: Many of the most cunning did not die; several thousand still remained.
translations.idiomatic: The craftiest survived; several thousand rebels remained.

sentences.zh: 金急欲成功，遂下令招撫。

translations.literal: Jin, urgent for success, then ordered pacification by recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to declare victory, Jin ordered offers of surrender.

sentences.zh: 其破姚源賊也，金喜，謂功在旦夕，與將吏置酒高會。

translations.literal: When he broke the Yaoyuan bandits Jin rejoiced, thinking merit was within days, and feasted with officers.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking the Yaoyuan rebels Jin rejoiced, thinking victory was days away, and feasted with his officers.

sentences.zh: 賊覘諸要害無守者，乃悉所有賂目兵，乘暮遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits spied that key points were unguarded, then bribed the native troops with all they had and fled at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw the passes unguarded, bribed the native troops with everything they had, and fled at dusk.

sentences.zh: 時賊絕爨已三日，自分必死，沿途棄稚弱，散婦女。

translations.literal: The bandits had gone three days without cooking fires and thought themselves doomed; along the way they abandoned infants and scattered women.
translations.idiomatic: Starving for three days and sure of death, they abandoned children and cast off women along the road.

sentences.zh: 及抵貴溪，始得一飽食，遂轉掠衢、徽間。

translations.literal: Only when they reached Guixi did they get a full meal, then turned to raid between Qu and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At Guixi they ate their first full meal, then swept through Quzhou and Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 金知失策，亦下令招降。

translations.literal: Jin, knowing he had erred, also ordered pacification by recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing his mistake, Jin again proclaimed surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊首王浩八等故偽降以緩官兵，攻剽如故，卒不能盡賊。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs such as Wang Haoba had formerly feigned surrender to slow government troops and raided as before; in the end the bandits could not be wholly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs like Wang Haoba had feigned surrender to stall the army and kept raiding; the rebels were never fully destroyed.

sentences.zh: 紀功給事中黎奭及兩京言官交章劾金。

translations.literal: Merit-recording supervising secretary Li Shuang and remonstrating officials of both capitals memorialized against Jin in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Merit secretary Li Shuang and censors of both capitals impeached Jin in turn.

sentences.zh: 乃召金還，以俞諫代。

translations.literal: Jin was then recalled and Yu Jian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Jin and sent Yu Jian in his place.

sentences.zh: 金遂請終喪去。

translations.literal: Jin then asked to complete his mourning and leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin asked to finish mourning and retire.

sentences.zh: 十年再起，督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled again to supervise military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled to direct the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 府江賊王公珣等為亂，金集諸道兵偕總兵官郭勛等分六路討之，斬公珣，大有所俘獲。

translations.literal: Fujiang bandit Wang Gongxun and others made trouble; Jin gathered troops from all circuits with overall commander Guo Xun and others to attack on six routes, beheaded Gongxun, and took many captives.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujiang rebel Wang Gongxun rose; Jin gathered forces under Guo Xun on six routes, slew Gongxun, and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 加少保太子太保，蔭子如初。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his son received hereditary privilege as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the same hereditary honors for his son.

sentences.zh: 復以饒平捷，詔子先受蔭者進一秩。

translations.literal: Again, for victory at Raoping, an edict advanced by one rank the son who had earlier received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: After victory at Raoping, the son already ennobled was advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 金承召還朝，道得疾歸，詔強起之。

translations.literal: Jin, on the road back to court after recall, fell ill and returned home; an edict ordered him forcibly recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he fell ill on the road and went home; the throne ordered him back despite illness.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬入掌都察院事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year's winter he entered to direct the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year he took charge of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，請老，命乘傳還。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded he asked to retire; he was ordered to return by post horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he asked to retire and was sent home by imperial post.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 俞諫，字良佐，桐廬人。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, styled Liangzuo, was a native of Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, whose style was Liangzuo, came from Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 父藎，舉進士，官御史，按江西，治外戚王氏、萬氏宗族恣橫罪。

translations.literal: His father Jin passed the jinshi, served as censor, inspected Jiangxi, and punished the crimes of the Wang and Wan clans of imperial affines for wanton violence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin became a jinshi, served as censor in Jiangxi, and punished the Wang and Wan clans of imperial in-laws for their violence.

sentences.zh: 坐事，謫澧州判官。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a court offense he was banished to serve as assistant magistrate of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 大築陂堰，溉田可萬頃。

translations.literal: He greatly built dikes and weirs, irrigating fields of up to ten thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: He built great dikes and weirs that irrigated fields of ten thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄖陽知府。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to prefect of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become prefect of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 諫舉弘治三年進士，授長清知縣，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Jian passed the jinshi in the third year of Hongzhi, was appointed magistrate of Changqing, and promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian passed the jinshi in the third year of Hongzhi, became magistrate of Changqing, and rose to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 遷河南僉事，擒嵩賊呂梅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan vice commissioner and captured Song bandit Lü Mei.
translations.idiomatic: As Henan vice commissioner he captured the Song bandit Lü Mei.

sentences.zh: 歷江西參議，平大帽山賊。

translations.literal: He served through Jiangxi vice commissioner and pacified the Great Hat Mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangxi vice commissioner and pacified the Great Hat Mountain rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東副使，中道召為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong vice commissioner; mid-journey he was summoned as vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner, he was summoned on the road to be vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 正德六年擢右僉都御史，治水蘇、杭諸府，修治圩塘，民享其利。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief, managed waterworks in Suzhou, Hangzhou, and other prefectures, repaired polders and dikes, and the people enjoyed the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengde he became Right Vice Censor-in-chief, managed waterworks across Suzhou and Hangzhou, repaired dikes and polders, and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 尋進右副都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and superintended river defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Vice Censor-in-chief and put in charge of river defense.

sentences.zh: 八年春，姚源降賊王浩八叛，詔以諫代陳金督江西、浙江、福建諸軍討之。

translations.literal: In spring of the eighth year the surrendered Yaoyuan bandit Wang Haoba rebelled; an edict made Jian replace Chen Jin to supervise troops of Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Fujian in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's spring the surrendered rebel Wang Haoba of Yaoyuan rose again; Jian was sent to replace Chen Jin and command Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時浩八眾萬余，屯浙江開化，為同知伍文定等所敗，遁還江西德興，以所執都指揮白弘、江洪為質，求撫於按察使王秩。

translations.literal: At this time Haoba's host exceeded ten thousand, encamped at Kaihua in Zhejiang, was defeated by Assistant Prefect Wu Wending and others, fled back to Dexing in Jiangxi, and with captured Commanders Bai Hong and Jiang Hong as hostages sought pacification from Vice Commissioner Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Haoba commanded over ten thousand men at Kaihua in Zhejiang, was beaten by Wu Wending, fled to Dexing in Jiangxi, and with captured commanders Bai Hong and Jiang Hong as hostages begged Wang Zhi for peace.

sentences.zh: 秩受之，為傳送姚源。

translations.literal: Zhi accepted them and had them escorted to Yaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi accepted and sent them on to Yaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 浩八奔據貴溪裴源山，余眾復集，連營十里。

translations.literal: Haoba fled to hold Peiyuan Mountain in Guixi; the remnant gathered again in camps ten li long.
translations.idiomatic: Haoba fled to Peiyuan Mountain in Guixi; survivors regrouped in a ten-li chain of camps.

sentences.zh: 諫令秩與副使胡世寧、參政吳廷舉列屯要害，斷其歸路，而躬與都督李鋐乘夜冒雨潛進。

translations.literal: Jian ordered Zhi with Vice Commissioner Hu Shining and Administration Commissioner Wu Tingju to camp at key points and cut their retreat, while he himself with Regional Commander Li Gang advanced by night through rain in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Jian posted Zhi, Hu Shining, and Wu Tingju at choke points to cut retreat while he and Regional Commander Li Gang stole forward through rain by night.

sentences.zh: 大破之，俘斬數千人，遂擒浩八。

translations.literal: He routed them severely, capturing and slaying several thousand, and then seized Haoba.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered them, killing or capturing thousands, and took Haoba.

sentences.zh: 其黨潰走玉山。

translations.literal: Their followers fled in collapse toward Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant fled toward Yushan.

sentences.zh: 諫與南贛巡撫周南、江西巡撫任漢復擊斬七百余人。

translations.literal: Jian with Grand Coordinators Zhou Nan of southern Gan and Ren Han of Jiangxi again struck and slew more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Coordinators Zhou Nan and Ren Han, Jian killed over seven hundred more.

sentences.zh: 余賊奔姚源，諫督廷舉等進剿，逼擒之。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled to Yaoyuan; Jian supervised Tingju and others in advance suppression and forced their capture.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors ran to Yaoyuan; Jian drove Tingju forward until they were taken.

sentences.zh: 諫懲金失，一意用兵，而任漢懦。

translations.literal: Jian, resenting Jin's failures, was bent on military action, while Ren Han was timid.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming Jin's failures, Jian insisted on force, while Ren Han was timid.

sentences.zh: 先為布政使，嘗贊金主撫。

translations.literal: Han had earlier been administration commissioner and had supported Jin's advocacy of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Han had once been administration commissioner and had backed Jin's preference for pacification.

sentences.zh: 雖亟上首功，追賊緩，余當復起。

translations.literal: Though he urgently reported first merit, pursuit of bandits was slow and the rest would rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Though he hurried victory reports, pursuit was slack and the rebels would regather.

sentences.zh: 先是，東鄉賊為金所敗乞降，隸世寧，號新兵，而剽掠如故。

translations.literal: Earlier the Dongxiang bandits, defeated by Jin, had begged to surrender and were placed under Shining as "new troops," yet they plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang rebels beaten by Jin had surrendered to Shining as "new troops" but kept looting.

sentences.zh: 既懼罪復叛，遣參將桂勇等討擒之。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment they rebelled again; Assistant Commander Gui Yong and others were sent to pursue and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment they rebelled again until Gui Yong and others hunted them down.

sentences.zh: 萬年雖立縣，賊尚眾，吏胥多賊黨，官府動息必知之。

translations.literal: Though Wannian county had been established, bandits were still numerous; clerks were often bandit accomplices, and the government's every move was known to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian county existed in name, but rebels remained numerous, clerks were often their spies, and officials' plans were known at once.

sentences.zh: 副使李情治峻急，眾欲叛，畏鋐在余幹不敢發。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Li Qing governed harshly; the masses wished to rebel but feared Gang was at Yugan and dared not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Li Qing ruled harshly; people meant to rebel but dared not while Li Gang held Yugan.

sentences.zh: 會鋐卒，王垂七、胡念二等遂作亂。

translations.literal: When Gang died, Wang Chuiqi, Hu Nianer, and others then made trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After Gang died, Wang Chuiqi and Hu Nianer rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 殺情及饒州通判陳達、秦碧，指揮邢世臣等，焚廨舍。

translations.literal: They killed Qing and Raozhou Assistant Prefect Chen Da and Qin Bi, Commander Xing Shichen, and others, and burned government offices.
translations.idiomatic: They slew Li Qing, Raozhou officials Chen Da and Qin Bi, Commander Xing Shichen, and others, and burned the yamen.

sentences.zh: 諫發兵擒之，亂乃定。

translations.literal: Jian sent troops and captured them; the turmoil was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent troops, seized them, and the disturbance ended.

sentences.zh: 言官劾諫及漢、南。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials impeached Jian as well as Han and Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached Jian along with Han and Nan.

sentences.zh: 兵部請召漢還，命諫兼領巡撫。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War asked to recall Han and ordered Jian to concurrently hold the grand coordinator post.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War recalled Han and let Jian serve concurrently as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 明年擊臨川賊，斬其魁，而遣參將李隆擊新淦賊。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked bandits in Linchuan, beheaded their chiefs, and sent Assistant Commander Li Long against bandits in Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he struck Linchuan rebels, beheaded their chiefs, and sent Li Long against Xingan.

sentences.zh: 賊踞萬山中，僭稱王且八年。

translations.literal: The bandits held the myriad mountains and had presumptuously styled themselves kings for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: They held the deep mountains and had called themselves kings for eight years.

sentences.zh: 隆等深入，悉就擒，俘斬千七百余人。

translations.literal: Long and others penetrated deeply; all were captured; more than one thousand seven hundred were taken or slain.
translations.idiomatic: Long drove deep inland and took them all, killing or capturing over one thousand seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進諫右都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded: Jian was advanced to Right Censor-in-chief, his grand coordinator post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For merit Jian was made Right Censor-in-chief while keeping his grand coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 劇賊徐九齡者，初嘯聚建昌、醴源。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Xu Jiuling had first gathered at Jianchang and Liyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The formidable rebel Xu Jiuling had first gathered in Jianchang and Liyuan.

sentences.zh: 已，出沒江、湖間，積三十年。

translations.literal: Later he ranged between the Yangzi and lakes, accumulating thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he roamed the Yangzi region for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 黃州、德安、九江、安慶、池州、太平鹹被其害。

translations.literal: Huangzhou, De'an, Jiujiang, Anqing, Chizhou, and Taiping all suffered his harm.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou, De'an, Jiujiang, Anqing, Chizhou, and Taiping all suffered at his hands.

sentences.zh: 諫討斬之，群盜悉平。

translations.literal: Jian campaigned against and beheaded him; all bandit groups were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jian hunted him down and beheaded him, and the remaining bands were pacified.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠諷御史張鰲山劾諫，十一年召還，遂乞致仕。

translations.literal: Prince of Ning Chen Hao prompted Investigating Censor Zhang Aoshan to impeach Jian; in the eleventh year he was recalled and then asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning Chen Hao prompted Zhang Aoshan to impeach Jian; in the eleventh year he was recalled and retired.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，用薦起故官，總督漕運。

translations.literal: At the change to Jiajing, on recommendation he was recalled to his former office to superintend grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiajing began he was recommended back to superintend grain transport.

sentences.zh: 青州礦盜王堂等起顏神鎮，流劫東昌、兗州、濟南。

translations.literal: Qingzhou mining bandits Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen town and raided through Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou mine rebels Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen and raided Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.

sentences.zh: 都指揮楊紀及指揮楊浩等擊之，浩死，紀僅免。

translations.literal: Commander Yang Ji and Commander Yang Hao and others attacked them; Hao died and Ji barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yang Ji and Commander Yang Hao attacked; Hao was killed and Ji barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔責山東將吏，於是諸臣分道逐賊，賊不復屯聚，流劫金鄉、魚臺間。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Shandong officers; then the various ministers pursued the bandits on separate routes; the bandits no longer camped together but raided between Jinxiang and Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked Shandong commanders; ministers pursued on separate routes; the rebels stopped camping together and raided between Jinxiang and Yutai.

sentences.zh: 突曹州，欲渡河不得，復掠考城並河西岸，至東明、長垣。

translations.literal: They burst into Caozhou, could not cross the river, again raided the west bank of the examination route through Kaocheng, and reached Dongming and Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Caozhou, failed to cross the river, swept the west bank through Kaocheng, and reached Dongming and Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 河南及保定守臣鹹告急。

translations.literal: Henan and Baoding defending officials all reported emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Baoding officials all cried for help.

sentences.zh: 賊黨王友賢等轉掠祥符、封丘，南抵徐州。

translations.literal: Bandit follower Wang Youxian and others turned to raid Xiangfu and Fengqiu, reaching south to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Wang Youxian and others raided Xiangfu and Fengqiu and pushed south to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷議以諸道巡撫權位相埒，乃命諫與都督魯綱並提督兩畿、山東、河南軍務，以便宜節制諸道兵討之。

translations.literal: Court debate held that the various grand coordinators' ranks were equal; Jian and Regional Commander Lu Gang were therefore ordered jointly to superintend military affairs in the two capital regions, Shandong, and Henan, with discretionary authority to command the various routes' troops in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Because grand coordinators held equal rank, the court ordered Jian and Regional Commander Lu Gang jointly to direct the two capital regions, Shandong, and Henan, with full power to command all routes against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊復流至考城。

translations.literal: The bandits again flowed to Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swept back toward Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 官軍方欲擊，而河南降賊張進引三百騎馳至。

translations.literal: Government troops were about to strike when the Henan surrendered bandit Zhang Jin led three hundred horsemen galloping up.
translations.idiomatic: As government forces prepared to attack, the Henan turncoat Zhang Jin arrived at a gallop with three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 中都留守顏愷與俱前，方戰，進忽三麾其旗先卻。

translations.literal: Central Capital garrison commander Yan Kai advanced with him; just as battle joined, Jin suddenly thrice waved his banner and withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: Central Capital commander Yan Kai marched with him; in the midst of battle Jin suddenly waved his standard three times and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 賊乘之，官軍大潰，將士死者八百余人。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the moment; government troops were utterly routed and more than eight hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the advantage; government troops collapsed, and more than eight hundred officers and men were killed.

sentences.zh: 諫等連營進，賊始滅。

translations.literal: Jian and others advanced in linked camps, and only then were the bandits extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pressed forward in linked camps until the rebels were finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其秋，召掌都察院事。

translations.literal: That autumn he was summoned to direct the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: That fall he was recalled to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒官，贈太子太保，謚莊襄。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the title Zhuangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died in post and was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Zhuangxiang.

sentences.zh: 周南，字文化，縉雲人。

translations.literal: Zhou Nan, styled Wenhua, was a native of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan, whose style was Wenhua, came from Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除六合知縣，擢御史，出按畿輔。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Liuhe, promoted to censor, and went out to inspect the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Liuhe, rose to censor, and inspected the home provinces.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，再按廣東，劾總兵官柳景。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he again inspected Guangdong and impeached overall commander Liu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he inspected Guangdong again and impeached Commander Liu Jing.

sentences.zh: 歷江西右布政使，擢右副都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: He served through Jiangxi Right Provincial Administration Commissioner and was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiangxi right provincial administration commissioner, then Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 武宗初立，寇入宣府，參將陳雄等邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong first acceded, raiders entered Xuanfu; Assistant Commander Chen Xiong and others intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzong's accession raiders entered Xuanfu; Assistant Commander Chen Xiong and others beat them back.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增南俸一秩，母喪歸。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; his southern salary was increased one rank, and he returned home for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For merit his southern salary rose one rank; then his mother died and he went into mourning.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，劉瑾擅政，以大同倉粟有浥爛者，逮南及督糧郎中孫祿下詔獄，械送大同，責倍輸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde Liu Jin monopolized government; because Datong granary grain had been soaked and spoiled, Nan and grain-supervising Director Sun Lu were seized and sent to the imperial prison, shackled and escorted to Datong, and charged to pay double.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde's third year Liu Jin ruled alone; spoiled grain at the Datong depot brought Nan and Director Sun Lu to the imperial prison, shackled to Datong, and ordered to pay double restitution.

sentences.zh: 會赦，大同總兵官葉椿等為請，免其倍數。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came, Datong overall commander Ye Chun and others pleaded for them and the double payment was waived.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty followed; Commander Ye Chun of Datong pleaded for them and the double levy was dropped.

sentences.zh: 輸畢，釋為民。

translations.literal: When payment was finished they were released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fine was paid they were released as civilians.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，以故官撫宣府不就，引病歸。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed he was offered his former post to grand coordinate Xuanfu but would not accept and cited illness to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was offered his old post at Xuanfu but refused and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年起督南、贛軍務。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled to supervise southern Gan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to direct military affairs in southern Gan.

sentences.zh: 南贛巡撫之設，自南始。

translations.literal: The establishment of the southern Gan grand coordinator post began with Nan.
translations.idiomatic: The office of southern Gan grand coordinator began with him.

sentences.zh: 汀州大帽山賊張時旺、黃鏞、劉隆、李四仔等聚眾稱王，攻剽城邑，延及江西、廣東之境，數年不靖，官軍討之輒敗。

translations.literal: On Great Hat Mountain in Tingzhou the bandits Zhang Shiwang, Huang Yong, Liu Long, Li Sizai, and others gathered, styled themselves kings, attacked and raided cities and towns, and extended into Jiangxi and Guangdong; for years they were not pacified and government troops were repeatedly defeated in campaigns against them.
translations.idiomatic: At Tingzhou's Great Hat Mountain, Zhang Shiwang, Huang Yong, Liu Long, Li Sizai, and others gathered, proclaimed themselves kings, raided towns across Jiangxi and Guangdong, and for years defied government troops who marched against them only to lose.

sentences.zh: 推官莫仲昭、知縣蔣璣、指揮楊澤等被執，賊勢愈熾。

translations.literal: Assistant Prefect Mo Zhongzhao, Magistrate Jiang Ji, Commander Yang Ze, and others were seized, and bandit strength grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Prefect Mo Zhongzhao, Magistrate Jiang Ji, and Commander Yang Ze were taken prisoner, and the rebels grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 南集諸道兵擊之龍牙，擒時旺。

translations.literal: Nan gathered troops from all circuits and attacked them at Longya, capturing Shiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Nan assembled forces from every circuit, struck at Longya, and captured Shiwang.

sentences.zh: 義民林富別擊斬鏞於鐵坑。

translations.literal: Righteous citizen Lin Fu separately attacked and beheaded Yong at Tiekeng.
translations.idiomatic: A local volunteer, Lin Fu, separately attacked and beheaded Yong at Tiekeng.

sentences.zh: 其他諸寨為指揮孫堂等所破。

translations.literal: The other stockades were broken by Commander Sun Tang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Sun Tang and others overran the remaining stockades.

sentences.zh: 而副使楊璋、僉事淩相等亦擊隆、四仔，擒之。
