translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Yang Zhang, Vice Commissioner Ling Xiang, and others also struck Long and Sizai and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioners Yang Zhang and Ling Xiang also attacked Long and Sizai and took them.

sentences.zh: 先後斬獲五千人，仲昭等得逸還。

translations.literal: In all five thousand were beheaded or captured, and Zhongzhao and the others escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand were killed or captured in all, and Zhongzhao and the rest made their way back alive.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, sealed letters of praise and reward were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Victory dispatches brought sealed praise from the throne.

sentences.zh: 南乃移師會總督陳金，共平姚源諸賊，境內遂寧。

translations.literal: Nan then shifted his army to join overall commander Chen Jin in jointly pacifying the Yaoyuan bandits, and the territory was then quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Nan then marched to join Grand Coordinator Chen Jin, together pacifying the Yaoyuan rebels until the region was calm.

sentences.zh: 九年春，進右都御史，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: In spring of the ninth year he was advanced to Right Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year's spring he became Right Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 逾年乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he begged to retire and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to retire and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 孫祿，棲霞人。

translations.literal: Sun Lu was a native of Qixia.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lu came from Qixia.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由戶部主事歷郎中。

translations.literal: From secretary in the Ministry of Revenue he rose through director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，起故官，累遷至應天府尹。

translations.literal: When Jin fell he was restored to his former office and rose through posts to prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored and eventually became prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 馬昊，本姓鄒，字宗大，寧夏人。

translations.literal: Ma Hao, original surname Zou, styled Zongda, was a native of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Hao, born Zou, whose style was Zongda, came from Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由行人選御史。

translations.literal: From courier he was selected as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a courier and was chosen censor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，遷山東僉事，坐累謫真定推官。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde he was transferred to Shandong vice commissioner; for an offense he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he became Shandong vice commissioner, then was demoted to assistant magistrate of Zhending for an offense.

sentences.zh: 境內數有盜，昊教吏士習射，廣設方略，盜發輒獲。

translations.literal: Bandits arose repeatedly in the jurisdiction; Hao taught clerks and scholars archery, broadly laid plans, and whenever bandits appeared they were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were frequent in his district; he trained clerks and students in archery, laid many stratagems, and seized rebels whenever they struck.

sentences.zh: 再坐累謫判開州。

translations.literal: Again for an offense he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again, to assistant magistrate of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 真定吏民伏闕請留，乃免。

translations.literal: Zhending clerks and people prostrated themselves at the palace gate begging he be kept; he was then spared.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhending knelt at the palace gates to keep him; the demotion was canceled.

sentences.zh: 遷四川僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Sichuan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Sichuan vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昊長身驍捷，善騎射，知兵。

translations.literal: Hao was tall in stature, fierce and agile, skilled at riding and archery, and knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was tall and quick, a fine horseman and archer who understood war.

sentences.zh: 巨寇方四、曹甫等方熾，洪鐘討之久無功。

translations.literal: Great bandits Fang Si, Cao Fu, and others were then at their height; Hong Zhong campaigned against them for long without success.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebels Fang Si and Cao Fu were at their peak; Hong Zhong had campaigned against them for years without success.

sentences.zh: 昊至，閱所部，笑曰：「將不知兵，其何以戰？

translations.literal: When Hao arrived he reviewed his command and laughed: "Generals who do not know warfare — how can they fight?
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he inspected his troops and laughed: "Generals who do not know war — how can they fight?"

sentences.zh: 」於是擇健卒千人分數隊，隊立長，教之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he chose a thousand stalwart soldiers, divided them into several companies, set a chief for each company, and trained them.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a thousand strong soldiers, divided them into companies with captains, and drilled them hard.

sentences.zh: 會甫將襲江津，昊從巡撫林俊剿賊，大敗之，俘斬及焚死者二千余人。

translations.literal: When Fu was about to strike Jiangjin, Hao followed Grand Coordinator Lin Jun in suppressing bandits and routed them severely, capturing, slaying, and burning more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: As Fu prepared to strike Jiangjin, Hao joined Grand Coordinator Lin Jun, crushed the rebels, and killed, captured, or burned more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年，方四陷江津，破綦江，薄重慶。

translations.literal: The next year Fang Si took Jiangjin, broke Qijiang, and pressed on Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Fang Si seized Jiangjin, overran Qijiang, and threatened Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 昊夜出百騎，舉火擊賊，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Hao led a hundred horsemen out by night, raised fires, and struck the bandits; the bandits fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Hao led a hundred horsemen out at night with torches, struck the rebels, and sent them fleeing in panic.

sentences.zh: 乘之，斬獲多，遂合羅、回土兵博賊。

translations.literal: Pressing the pursuit he slew and captured many, then joined Luo and Hui native troops to grapple with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit, took many heads, then joined Luo and Hui native levies to close with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊陳左而伏兵其右，昊以正兵當左，身率百騎搗其伏。

translations.literal: The bandits deployed on the left while ambush troops lay on the right; Hao met the left with the main force and personally led a hundred horsemen to smash the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels formed on the left with an ambush on the right; Hao held the left with his main body and personally led a hundred horsemen against the trap.

sentences.zh: 伏潰，趨左，左亦潰，四奔婺川，與甫相攻，眾遂散。

translations.literal: The ambush collapsed; he rushed the left, the left also collapsed, Si fled to Wuchuan, fought with Fu, and the host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush broke; he wheeled on the left wing and broke it too; Si fled to Wuchuan, clashed with Fu, and the rebel host scattered.

sentences.zh: 四變姓名走，為他將所獲。

translations.literal: Si changed his name and fled but was captured by another commander.
translations.idiomatic: Si changed his name and ran, only to be taken by another commander.

sentences.zh: 昊再被獎，進副使，與總兵官楊宏擊敗甫。

translations.literal: Hao was again rewarded and promoted to vice commissioner; with overall commander Yang Hong he defeated Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded again, Hao was made vice commissioner and, with Commander Yang Hong, broke Fu's force.

sentences.zh: 甫降，而其黨廖麻子並其眾，連陷銅梁、榮昌。

translations.literal: Fu surrendered, but his follower Liao Mazi absorbed his host and in succession took Tongliang and Rongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu surrendered, but Liao Mazi took over his band and seized Tongliang and Rongchang in turn.

sentences.zh: 坐奪冠帶。

translations.literal: For this he was stripped of his cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank for the loss.

sentences.zh: 時洪鐘已召還，巡撫高崇熙恇怯，復主撫。

translations.literal: At this time Hong Zhong had already been recalled; Grand Coordinator Gao Chongxi was timid and again favored pacification.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hong Zhong was gone; the new grand coordinator Gao Chongxi was timid and favored negotiation again.

sentences.zh: 麻子等陽受約，崇熙遽罷諸軍，令副使張敏徙開縣臨江市民，空其地處之，許給復三年，為請於朝。

translations.literal: Mazi and others outwardly accepted terms; Chongxi hastily disbanded the armies and ordered Vice Commissioner Zhang Min to move the market people of Linjiang in Kaixian, empty the land to settle them, grant tax relief for three years, and memorialize the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mazi and the rest pretended to submit; Chongxi hurriedly dismissed the armies and told Vice Commissioner Zhang Min to evacuate Linjiang marketfolk in Kaixian, clear the land for the rebels, grant three years' tax relief, and petition the court.

sentences.zh: 昊力爭，謂臨江市蜀襟喉，上達重、敘，下連湖、湘，地土饒衍，奈何棄以資賊，自遺患。

translations.literal: Hao struggled fiercely against it, saying Linjiang was the throat of Shu, reaching Chong and Xu above and Huguang and Hunan below, with rich land — how abandon it to bandits and invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Hao protested fiercely: Linjiang was Shu's throat, linking Chongqing and Xuzhou above with Huguang and Hunan below on rich soil — to abandon it to rebels was to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 崇熙不從，昊乃益治兵觀變。

translations.literal: Chongxi would not listen; Hao then trained troops all the more and watched for changes.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi refused; Hao redoubled his training and watched how events would turn.

sentences.zh: 其明年，賊果執敏叛。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits indeed seized Min and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels seized Zhang Min and rose again.

sentences.zh: 詔逮崇熙，而擢昊右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: An edict seized Chongxi and promoted Hao to Right Vice Censor-in-chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi was arrested and Hao promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 賊圍中江，將趨成都。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged Zhongjiang and were about to press on Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged Zhongjiang and aimed at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 昊以五千騎與總督彭澤敗之。

translations.literal: Hao with five thousand horsemen joined Grand Coordinator Peng Ze and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao led five thousand horsemen, joined Peng Ze, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 遊擊閻勛追斬麻子劍州，余眾走，推其黨喻思俸為主。

translations.literal: Guerrilla officer Yan Xun pursued and beheaded Mazi at Jianzhou; the remnant fled and made his follower Yu Sibo leader.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla Yan Xun ran Mazi down and killed him at Jianzhou; survivors fled and raised Yu Sibo as chief.

sentences.zh: 總兵官陳珣追至富村，賊偽降。

translations.literal: Overall commander Chen Xun pursued to Fucun and the bandits feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chen Xun pursued to Fucun, where the rebels pretended to surrender.

sentences.zh: 因北渡江，襲殺都指揮姚震，轉入巴山故巢。

translations.literal: They then crossed the river north, made a surprise attack and killed Commander-in-chief Yao Zhen, and turned into the old lair in Ba Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed north, ambushed and killed Commander Yao Zhen, and withdrew into their old Ba Mountain stronghold.

sentences.zh: 尋出走大安鎮，珣不敢前。

translations.literal: Soon they went out again to Da'an town; Xun dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they broke out toward Da'an; Xun would not advance.

sentences.zh: 而陜西兵與賊戰潰，賊遂越寧羌犯略陽。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shaanxi troops were routed in battle with the bandits; the bandits then crossed Ningqiang and invaded Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi troops were beaten; the rebels crossed Ningqiang and struck Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 珣軍鼓噪，賊夜走，度廣元，為官軍所遏，還趨通、巴招余黨。

translations.literal: Xun's army clamored and the bandits fled by night, crossed Guangyuan, were blocked by government troops, turned back toward Tong and Ba to recruit the remnant.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's men raised a din; the rebels fled by night, were blocked at Guangyuan, and turned back toward Tong and Ba to gather survivors.

sentences.zh: 諸將率稱病不擊賊，詔逮珣，且讓昊。

translations.literal: The various commanders mostly claimed illness and would not strike the bandits; an edict seized Xun and also rebuked Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders mostly pleaded illness and would not fight; Xun was arrested and Hao rebuked.

sentences.zh: 昊乃與彭澤督諸軍獲思俸西鄉山中，復與澤平內江賊駱松祥，群盜悉靖。

translations.literal: Hao then with Peng Ze supervised the various armies in capturing Sibo in the mountains of Xixiang, and again with Ze pacified the Neijiang bandit Luo Songxiang; all bandit groups were then quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Peng Ze then took Sibo in the Xixiang hills and crushed the Neijiang rebel Luo Songxiang; every band was pacified.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進副都御史。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and he was advanced to Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十年，亦不剌寇松藩，番人磨讓六少等乘機亂，為之向導，西土大震。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Ibrahim raided Songpan; the Tibetan Mo Rangliushao and others took advantage of the disorder to make trouble, acting as guides, and the western regions were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Ibrahim raided Songpan; Tibetan chiefs including Mo Rangliushao stirred rebellion as guides, and the western frontier shook.

sentences.zh: 昊招土番為間，發兵掩擊之。

translations.literal: Hao recruited native Tibetans as agents and sent troops in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Hao turned native Tibetans as spies and launched a surprise strike.

sentences.zh: 千戶張倫等夜率熟番攻破賊，獲磨讓六少，亦不剌遁去。

translations.literal: Company commander Zhang Lun and others led acculturated Tibetans by night to break the bandits, captured Mo Rangliushao, and Ibrahim fled.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion Zhang Lun led loyal Tibetans in a night assault, seized Mo Rangliushao, and Ibrahim fled.

sentences.zh: 昊以松潘地險阻，番人往往邀劫饋運，乃督參將張傑等修築墻柵，自三舍堡至風洞關，凡五十里。

translations.literal: Hao, because Songpan terrain was perilous and Tibetans often intercepted supply transport, supervised Assistant Commander Zhang Jie and others in building wall palisades from Sanshe fort to Fengdong Pass, fifty li in all.
translations.idiomatic: Songpan's terrain was treacherous and Tibetans often ambushed supplies; Hao had Zhang Jie build palisades from Sanshe fort to Fengdong Pass, fifty li in all.

sentences.zh: 賜敕褒之。

translations.literal: Sealed letters of praise were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent sealed praise.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙、芒部二府壤接筠連、珙縣，圍亙千里，山箐深阻。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Wumeng and Mangbu bordered Junlian and Gong counties over a thousand li of deep mountain ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Wumeng and Mangbu prefectures adjoined Junlian and Gong across a thousand li of rugged mountains.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻僰人子、羿子、仲家子、苗子、倮、佫等雜居其中。

translations.literal: Various Yi peoples — Bozi, Yizi, Zhongjiazi, Miaozi, Luo, and Gela — lived intermingled there.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi, Yizi, Zhongjiazi, Miaozi, Luo, and Gela tribes lived intermingled throughout.

sentences.zh: 有僰人子普法惡者，通漢語，曉符錄。

translations.literal: Among the Bozi was one Pufa E, who knew Chinese and understood talismans and registers.
translations.idiomatic: A Bozi named Pufa E spoke Chinese and knew charms and registers.

sentences.zh: 妄言彌勒出世，自稱蠻王，煽諸夷作亂。

translations.literal: He falsely said Maitreya had appeared in the world, styled himself barbarian king, and incited the various tribes to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Maitreya had come, styled himself barbarian king, and incited the tribes to revolt.

sentences.zh: 流民謝文禮、謝文義應之。

translations.literal: Displaced people Xie Wenli and Xie Wenyi responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants Xie Wenli and Xie Wenyi joined him.

sentences.zh: 都指揮杜琮戰敗，文義奪其胄。

translations.literal: Commander Du Cong was defeated in battle; Wenyi seized his helmet.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Du Cong was routed; Wenyi took his helmet.

sentences.zh: 十二年，昊督指揮曹昱進討，法惡敗，走保青山寨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Hao supervised Commander Cao Yu in advance suppression; E was defeated and fled to hold Qingshan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Hao directed Commander Cao Yu against him; E was beaten and fled to Qingshan stockade.

sentences.zh: 昊分據水口，絕其汲道，闕南方圍待之。

translations.literal: Hao divided forces to hold the water mouths, cut off their water route, and left the south open in a surrounding wait.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized the water sources, cut off supply, and left the south open to lure them out.

sentences.zh: 賊乏水渴，突南圍，官軍遮擊。

translations.literal: The bandits lacked water and were thirsty; they burst through the southern encirclement and government troops intercepted and struck.
translations.idiomatic: Parched for water, the rebels charged the southern gap; government troops met them head-on.

sentences.zh: 法惡中流矢死，諸蠻大奔。

translations.literal: E was struck by an arrow and died; the various tribes fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: E took an arrow and died; the tribes broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 以功，再進右都御史，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was again advanced to Right Censor-in-chief; his son was ennobled hereditary commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Right Censor-in-chief again, and his son received hereditary rank in the Embroidered Uniform Guard for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 昊有才氣，能應變，揮霍自喜，所向輒有功。

translations.literal: Hao had talent and dash, could adapt to circumstances, was free-spending and pleased with himself, and wherever he went he generally won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and bold, adaptable and free-spending, Hao usually won wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 然官川中久，狎其俗，銳意立功名，卒以是敗。

translations.literal: Yet having long served in Sichuan he had grown familiar with its customs, was keen to establish fame and merit, and in the end failed for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yet long service in Sichuan had made him too familiar with local ways; his hunger for glory was what ruined him in the end.

sentences.zh: 先是，亦不剌既遁，昊移兵攻小東路番寨未下，茂州群蠻懼見侵，遂糾生苗圍城堡。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Ibrahim had fled, Hao shifted troops to attack the Lesser Eastern Route Tibetan stockades without taking them; the Maozhou tribes, fearing invasion, then rallied raw Miao to besiege castles.
translations.idiomatic: After Ibrahim fled, Hao attacked Lesser Eastern Route Tibetan stockades without success; fearing invasion, Maozhou tribes rallied raw Miao to besiege forts.

sentences.zh: 參將芮錫等討之，兵敗，指揮龐昇等皆死。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander Rui Xi and others campaigned against them; the army was defeated and Commander Pang Sheng and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Rui Xi marched against them, was routed, and Commander Pang Sheng and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遣副總兵張傑、副使吳澧擊松潘南北二路番，不利，亡軍士三千余人，匿不以聞。

translations.literal: He also once sent Deputy Commander Zhang Jie and Vice Commissioner Wu Li to strike the northern and southern route Tibetans of Songpan without success, losing more than three thousand soldiers, which he concealed and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent Zhang Jie and Wu Li against Songpan's northern and southern Tibetans, lost over three thousand men, and hid the defeat from court.

sentences.zh: 僰蠻平，不置戍守，遽班師。

translations.literal: When the Bo-Yi rebels were pacified he did not leave garrisons and hurriedly withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Bo rebels were beaten, he left no garrisons and rushed the army home.

sentences.zh: 請改高縣為州，設長吏，增高、珙、筠連田租千八百石，令指揮魏武度田奪降人業給之軍民。

translations.literal: He requested changing Gaoxian to a prefecture, setting chief officials, raising the land tax of Gao, Gong, and Junlian by one thousand eight hundred shi, and ordering Commander Wei Wu to survey fields and seize surrendered people's holdings to supply troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to elevate Gaoxian to a prefecture, appoint senior officials, raise land tax in Gao, Gong, and Junlian by one thousand eight hundred shi, and have Commander Wei Wu survey fields and strip surrendered people's land for troops and settlers.

sentences.zh: 而珙縣知縣步梁窺昊意，誘殺降人阿尚。

translations.literal: Gong county magistrate Bu Liang, divining Hao's intent, enticed and killed the surrendered man A Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Magistrate Bu Liang, reading Hao's mind, lured and killed the surrendered chief A Shang.

sentences.zh: 杜琮以亡胄故，怨文義，潛使人購其頭。

translations.literal: Du Cong, because of the lost helmet, resented Wenyi and secretly sent men to buy his head.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, shamed by the lost helmet, hated Wenyi and secretly put a price on his head.

sentences.zh: 於是文義乘群蠻怨，嗾之，遂大訌。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenyi took advantage of the various tribes' grievances and incited them, and great strife ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi played on the tribes' anger, stirred them up, and open rebellion followed.

sentences.zh: 攻高、慶符二縣，破其城。

translations.literal: They attacked Gao and Qingfu counties and broke their cities.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Gao and Qingfu and breached both county seats.

sentences.zh: 琮率兵禦之，又敗，死傷七百人。

translations.literal: Cong led troops to resist but was defeated again; seven hundred were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong marched to meet them, was beaten again, and lost seven hundred killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 自黎雅以西，天全六番皆相繼亂。

translations.literal: From Liya westward, the six fan divisions of Tianquan all rose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: West of Liya, the six Tianquan fan districts erupted one after another.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中孫懋暨巡按御史盧雍、黎龍先後劾昊。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretary Sun Mao and investigating censors Lu Yong and Li Long successively impeached Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Sun Mao and investigating censors Lu Yong and Li Long impeached Hao in turn.

sentences.zh: 十四年遂遣官逮昊。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year officials were finally sent to arrest Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the court at last sent officers to seize him.

sentences.zh: 行至河南，疏稱疾篤，留於家。

translations.literal: Reaching Henan, he memorialized that his illness was grave and remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Henan he pleaded grave illness and was left at home.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，始就逮，尋削籍歸。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded he was finally taken into custody, then was struck from the rolls and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Emperor Shizong succeeded was he taken; soon he was struck from the register and sent home.

sentences.zh: 楊一清、胡世寧薦之，為桂萼所駁而止。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing and Hu Shining recommended him, but Gui E rebuffed it and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing and Hu Shining urged his restoration, but Gui E blocked it and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：何鑒綰中樞，能任諸將滅賊，蓋其時楊廷和在政府，閣部同心，故克奏效雲爾。

translations.literal: The historian comments: He Jian held the central command and could employ generals to destroy bandits — largely because Yang Tinghe was in government and the court and ministries were of one mind, and so success could be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark that He Jian commanded the center and used his generals well because Yang Tinghe still led the government and court and ministries pulled together — only then could the campaigns succeed.

sentences.zh: 馬中錫雅負時望，而軍旅非其所長，適用取敗。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongxi bore high repute in his time, yet warfare was not his strength; placed in the wrong role he met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongxi enjoyed great literary fame, but armies were not his gift; put in command, he was bound to fail.

sentences.zh: 然觀劉宸阻降之言，亦可以觀朝事矣。

translations.literal: Yet observing Liu Chen's words blocking surrender, one may also observe the affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Liu Chen's refusal to accept surrender one can read the temper of the times at court.

sentences.zh: 陸完交結之罪浮於首功，得從八議，有佚罰焉。

translations.literal: Lu Wan's crime of collusion outweighed his chief merit in pacifying bandits; falling under the eight considerations, there was leniency in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan's treasonable dealings outweighed his service against the rebels; under the eight mitigations his punishment was softened — perhaps too softly.

sentences.zh: 洪鐘、陳金威略甚著，而土兵之謠，聞之心惻，斯又統戎旃者所當留意也。

translations.literal: Hong Zhong and Chen Jin had conspicuous martial achievement, yet the ballad of the native soldiers, heard, makes the heart ache — this too is what commanders of armies ought to heed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhong and Chen Jin won striking victories, yet the folk rhyme about native troops still wounds the ear — a warning any commander bearing the army standard should remember.
